social_history.living_situation: Lives alone; daughter checks in daily

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait disorder and cognitive decline attributed to 'back issues' — admitted for NPH evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: A 67-year-old right-handed woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity, and lumbar spinal stenosis was admitted for NPH evaluation after her outpatient neurologist identified ventriculomegaly on brain MRI obtained to evaluate cognitive concerns. The patient has had a progressive gait disorder over 12 months which she and her family attributed entirely to her known lumbar spinal stenosis. However, her spine surgeon noted that her gait pattern does not match typical lumbar stenosis neurogenic claudication (which typically worsens with standing/walking and improves with sitting/flexion — no such positional pattern is present). She has significant memory difficulties over the same period (HbA1c 8.4% — poorly controlled diabetes is a contributing factor per her endocrinologist). She has urinary incontinence on top of pre-existing urge incontinence from diabetes-related bladder dysfunction. MRI brain shows Evans index 0.30 (borderline) with callosal angle 91 degrees (just above 90 degree threshold — does not meet NPH criterion). MRI lumbar spine shows multilevel stenosis. The competing diagnoses (lumbar stenosis for gait, diabetes for cognition) make this a moderate-difficulty case.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x3. MoCA 21/30. Losses on attention, delayed recall, and executive function.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal upper extremity strength. Mild proximal lower extremity weakness 4+/5 bilaterally (could be diabetic amyotrophy vs lumbar stenosis). Lower extremity tone mildly increased.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reduced vibration and light touch bilateral feet (diabetic peripheral neuropathy pattern). Mild saddle anesthesia — lumbar stenosis component.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Patellar diminished bilaterally (2- vs 1+). Achilles absent bilaterally (diabetes/neuropathy). Plantar flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Short-stepped, wide-based, shuffling. Does NOT worsen with prolonged walking or improve with sitting forward (unlike lumbar stenosis neurogenic claudication). TUG 30 seconds. 10-meter walk 24 seconds.
neurological_exam.additional: No clonus. No upper motor neuron signs. Lumbar range of motion limited. Obesity complicates gait assessment.

mri.impression: 1. Brain MRI: Ventriculomegaly; Evans index 0.30. Callosal angle 91 degrees on coronal imaging. Moderate bilateral periventricular and subcortical white matter hyperintensity. 2. Lumbar MRI: Severe bilateral lateral recess stenosis at L3-4 and L4-5. Clinical correlation recommended.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Glucose 162 mg/dL (H), HbA1c 8.4 % (H), MMA 320 nmol/L (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 15 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 46 mg/dL. Glucose: 68 mg/dL (ratio 0.42). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 644 pg/mL (borderline low; reference >650). total_tau: 258 pg/mL (borderline elevated). phospho_tau: 48 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with gait analysis

findings.note: Gait quality post-tap: step height improved, less wide-based; lower extremity weakness persists (lumbar/diabetes component unchanged)

specialized_test.impression: High-volume tap trial (40 mL): TUG improved from 30 seconds pre-tap to 24 seconds at 24 hours (20% improvement). 10-meter walk improved from 24 to 19.5 seconds (19% improvement). MoCA improved 1 point at 24 hours. Post-tap gait: step height improved, less wide-based; lower extremity weakness component unchanged. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Extended lumbar drainage (72 hours): progressive gait improvement — TUG from 30 seconds baseline to 21 seconds at day 3 (30% improvement). Clinical correlation recommended.

Phase-contrast MRI (aqueductal CSF flow): peak velocity 19 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); net stroke volume 55 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Mildly hyperdynamic aqueductal CSF pulsatility identified. Clinical correlation recommended.
Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 20, below the amyloid positivity threshold. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: Impaired lower extremity — neuropathy and lumbar stenosis

quantitative_data.pattern: Multiple contributing factors: NPH frontal-subcortical + diabetic cognitive impairment + functional B12 deficiency

output.impression: Neuropsychological evaluation demonstrates severely impaired processing speed, moderately impaired executive function, mildly impaired episodic memory, and impaired sensory-motor function in lower extremities. Multiple contributors to cognitive and motor impairment are identified. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Concurrent diabetic bladder dysfunction — reduced bladder sensation

output.impression: Mixed urinary dysfunction: neurogenic detrusor overactivity with involuntary contractions and concurrent reduced bladder sensation pattern. No outlet obstruction. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: B12 supplementation 1000 mcg IM + continue metformin
interactions: Metformin reduces ileal B12 absorption — parenteral B12 bypasses this mechanism; continue metformin for diabetes management
warnings: Monitor B12 levels annually given ongoing metformin use
Oral B12 supplementation may be less effective given metformin-induced malabsorption — IM preferred initially
alternatives: High-dose oral B12 (1000-2000 mcg/day) as alternative if IM not tolerated

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Occasional premature atrial complexes, a benign finding. No acute ST-T changes.
ecg.interpretation: Largely normal ECG with a benign incidental finding

additional_observations: No acute intracranial haemorrhage, established infarct, mass, or midline shift.
Grey-white differentiation preserved; basal cisterns patent.
ct.impression: Non-contrast head CT without acute intracranial abnormality. CT is non-contributory to this evaluation and inferior to MRI for assessing ventricular morphometry (Evans index, callosal angle); clinical correlation with MRI recommended.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

cardiac_monitoring.rhythm_summary: Predominant sinus rhythm throughout the recording
findings: Brief runs of asymptomatic sinus tachycardia. No sustained arrhythmia, no pauses greater than 2 seconds, no AV block.
cardiac_monitoring.impression: 24-hour Holter monitor with only benign findings.

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / subcortical ischaemic vascular disease
differential.key_features: Small-vessel disease can produce gait apraxia and executive slowing, but ventriculomegaly out of proportion to white-matter burden and a positive tap test favour NPH
Shuffling gait overlaps, but absence of resting tremor, asymmetric rigidity, or L-dopa response and presence of magnetic gait + DESH favour NPH

Cognitive decline overlaps; AD typically presents with episodic-memory predominance and hippocampal atrophy rather than frontal-subcortical pattern and magnetic gait; CSF biomarkers / amyloid PET resolve copathology

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral atrophy with secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly
differential.key_features: Ventriculomegaly proportionate to sulcal widening, callosal angle >90°, and absence of DESH or transependymal signal argue against true NPH
No history of trauma, SAH, or meningitis on review; would be considered if history suggested antecedent intracranial event

optimal_actions.action: Literature review of iNPH diagnostic criteria and shunt-response predictors
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Relkin 2005 INPH Study Group criteria; Tisell 2011 tap-test predictors; Williams 2016 review

optimal_actions.action: Brain MRI — measure Evans index, callosal angle, assess DESH pattern; exclude mass effect, hydrocephalus from secondary cause, and atrophy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Ventriculomegaly with Evans index >0.3, DESH pattern (tight high-convexity sulci + widened Sylvian fissures), callosal angle <90°, periventricular transependymal signal; no mass effect or aqueductal obstruction

optimal_actions.action: Reversible-cause labs (TSH, B12, RPR, HIV) to exclude metabolic / infectious dementia mimics
optimal_actions.expected_finding: TSH, B12, RPR, HIV negative or within normal range; reversible mimics excluded

optimal_actions.action: Baseline neuropsychological battery — subcortical/frontal pattern, and reference for pre/post-tap comparison
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-subcortical pattern: executive dysfunction and slowed processing predominate over episodic amnesia

optimal_actions.action: Large-volume lumbar puncture (30-50 mL tap test) with opening pressure and pre/post gait + neuropsych assessment
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Opening pressure <25 cmH2O (normal); 30-50 mL CSF removed; pre/post tap gait and neuropsych assessment shows objective improvement supporting shunt-responsive iNPH

optimal_actions.action: Neurosurgery consultation for VP shunt candidacy and perioperative planning
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Neurosurgery accepts patient for VP shunt evaluation with programmable valve

optimal_actions.action: Amyloid PET (optional) — screen for AD copathology that may temper cognitive (but not gait) shunt benefit
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Inform shunt prognosis: AD copathology common (~50% iNPH)

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific for NPH and does not distinguish from neurodegenerative alternatives in this chronic gait/cognitive presentation
ECG is unrelated to the diagnostic workup of chronic gait + cognitive + urinary triad once cardiogenic syncope is not on the differential
Echocardiography does not contribute to NPH evaluation in the absence of syncope or cardioembolic stroke workup
Head CT is inferior to MRI for measuring Evans index and callosal angle and for excluding secondary causes; only justified if MRI is contraindicated
Cardiac monitoring has no diagnostic role in NPH and is reserved for syncope or arrhythmia workup

sequence_constraints.reason: MRI must precede large-volume LP to exclude mass effect or secondary obstructive hydrocephalus before removing 30-50 mL of CSF
Baseline neuropsychological and gait assessment must be obtained before the tap test so that pre/post change can be measured (tap response is the shunt-response predictor)

critical_actions: Obtain brain MRI before lumbar puncture to exclude mass effect or obstructive hydrocephalus
Document objective pre-tap gait (TUG and 10-metre walk) and neuropsychological baseline so that pre/post-tap change can be quantified
Remove 30-50 mL of CSF during the tap test (a low-volume LP under-samples and biases the test toward false negative)
Re-assess gait and cognition 1-4 hours after the tap and again at 24 hours (the response window for tap-test prediction of shunt benefit)
Refer to neurosurgery for VP shunt evaluation when imaging, clinical, and tap-test criteria support iNPH
contraindicated_actions: Do not perform large-volume lumbar puncture before MRI excludes mass effect or obstructive hydrocephalus
Do not infer iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone — DESH, callosal angle <90°, and a clinical triad are required
Do not diagnose Alzheimer's disease in a patient with gait-predominant presentation and ventriculomegaly without first excluding NPH
Do not attribute the syndrome to 'normal ageing' or 'deconditioning' once the imaging criteria for ventriculomegaly are met
key_reasoning_points: iNPH diagnosis (Relkin 2005 INPH Study Group) requires (a) Hakim's triad of gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary urgency/incontinence — gait is typically first and most prominent; (b) ventriculomegaly with Evans >0.3 and DESH on MRI without mass effect; (c) age >40 and chronic course; (d) opening pressure <25 cmH2O; (e) absence of an alternative explanation
MRI is the imaging modality of choice — measure Evans index and callosal angle (<90° supports NPH) and confirm DESH (tight high-convexity sulci + wide Sylvian fissures)

The tap test is a 30-50 mL large-volume LP with pre/post objective gait (TUG, 10-metre walk) and neuropsychological assessment; opening pressure must be normal (<25 cmH2O) to satisfy the 'normal pressure' criterion
Tap-test sensitivity is only 50-80%; a single negative tap does not exclude NPH — an extended (3-5 day) lumbar drainage trial can resolve borderline cases
Reversible-cause labs (TSH, B12, RPR, HIV) are mandatory before attributing the syndrome to NPH
Approximately 50% of iNPH patients have AD copathology — this lowers cognitive benefit from shunting but does not negate gait benefit
Shunt response is best predicted by an objectively positive tap test or extended drainage trial in a patient who meets imaging and clinical criteria

red_herrings.intended_effect: Gait limitation is attributed solely to lumbar stenosis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Lumbar stenosis produces position-dependent claudication, not magnetic gait or new ventriculomegaly with DESH

red_herrings.intended_effect: Gait ataxia is attributed to diabetic peripheral neuropathy
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Diabetic neuropathy produces sensory ataxia with reduced ankle vibration, not magnetic gait with freezing; ventriculomegaly + DESH indicate NPH

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Moderate NPH with multiple competing diagnoses: severe lumbar stenosis, poorly controlled diabetes, functional B12 deficiency (metformin), and vascular white matter disease — borderline imaging (Evans exactly 0.30, callosal angle 91).
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required tools (MRI, labs, neuropsych baseline, large-volume LP/tap, neurosurgery consult, literature), 2 grounded red herrings; differential includes 5 active alternatives. Pre-existing spinal pathology competes for attribution of gait decline.
vocab_gap: Phase-contrast (CSF flow) MRI is referenced in followup outputs but is not in the TOOL_PARAMETER_VOCABULARY closed list for order_advanced_imaging — recommend adding 'phase_contrast_MRI' or 'CSF_flow_MRI' to the modality vocabulary

Extended 72-hour external lumbar drainage trial is referenced in followup outputs but has no explicit key in TOOL_PARAMETER_VOCABULARY (currently subsumed under neuropsych_battery for the pre/post assessment) — recommend adding an explicit 'extended_lumbar_drainage' specialized_test key
